mechanisms.behavior: Four drop leaves stay closed when down. Solenoid 5 raises all four; clear leaves only as targets rise. The retained gameplay probe completed the bank and observed output 5. Reset retry timing and target animation are table-owned.
mechanisms.label: Attic Four-Target Bank

mechanisms.behavior: Five drop leaves stay closed when down. L13 drives booster Q3 and A-17891 to raise the bank. The probe's final down target produced L13; clear leaves on physical reset, not immediately on a hit.
mechanisms.label: Cellar Five-Target Bank

mechanisms.behavior: The cellar rear cup closes 31. L12 energizes A-20558 K relay, whose normally open contact applies 38V to separate A-21741 winding. The vertical plunger returns the ball to the main level and 31 opens after departure. The ROM probe raised L12 and cleared L17. Do not model the relay as the high-current winding itself.
mechanisms.label: Cellar Return Up-Kicker and K Relay

mechanisms.behavior: The lower/end cellar hole holds the ball on 41 until public 6 ejects it back onto the cellar. It is a separate device and path from the rear up-kicker 31.
mechanisms.label: Cellar Lower Special Hole

mechanisms.behavior: The main-level cup closes 45; output 2 drives A-5194's vertical plunger and wireform. Clear 45 as the ball leaves. The script's kick angle and delay are implementation tuning, not physical measurements; a callback name alone does not establish a cross-level destination.
mechanisms.label: Main-Level Vertical Up-Kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Ball occupancy closes 46; public 1 drives the hole kicker. This central hole differs from the left/right cellar-entry troughs 6/16. It is not a startup ball inventory merely because a script initializes 46.
mechanisms.label: Main Top-Center Hole

mechanisms.behavior: The right-side contact 65 requests L15. Q1 boosts the lamp-driver control into A-5195. Its spring/plunger throws the ball away from the right drain area. The impulse-plunger class used by the script is a simulation helper, not a motorized shooter plunger.
mechanisms.label: Right-Side Help Kicker

mechanisms.behavior: L16/Q2/A-17875 moves the hinged circular door through a lever, link and plunger; springs provide return action. Opening admits the ball into the separate trough 36 leading to the cellar. The local coil-side cutoff/hold contact has no public matrix address; 36 is the normally open trough leaf. Door plane, spring return and link topology are physical; script animation speed is not.
mechanisms.label: Hinged Trap Door and Trough

mechanisms.behavior: The main target face rocks on its fulcrum/shaft under ball force, letting the ball enter the hidden passage to the cellar; its spring returns the face. SW26 belongs to the downstream trough, not a target-position sensor. There is no separately commanded reset coil for this passive target.
mechanisms.label: Passive Secret Passage Roll-Down Target

mechanisms.behavior: The main drain closes 67 at the outhole. Solenoid 9 ejects the single ball into the manual shooter lane. No separate trough stack, automatic shooter coil or motor is documented. Table Kicker1..Kicker6 transport and configurable MaxBalls are recreation helpers; do not count them as fitted devices.
mechanisms.label: Single-Ball Outhole and Manual Shooter

mechanisms.behavior: Four pop-bumper driver boards respond to local switches: two main bumpers share 44, attic 43, cellar 1. Main kicking devices correspond to 14/24/25 and the kicking-rubber portion of 66; cellar kicking target 11 and the kicking-rubber portion of 51 are locally powered. Other 42/51/66 leaves only score. These coils are not public CPU solenoids; use physical switch/relay causality rather than inventing controller outputs. Their supply-enabling relays belong to the illumination/selection mechanism, not duplicate actuator instances.
mechanisms.label: Hardware-Wired Bumpers and Kicking Devices

mechanisms.behavior: Four main flippers are operated by the red cabinet buttons; two attic and two cellar flippers use the green buttons, with relay contacts enabling the cellar during cellar play. PinMAME exposes only the synthetic red-button pair 112/114 and outputs 45–48. Green inputs and EOS contacts are hardware-only, with no separate CPU address. The older retained table optionally couples button pairs and routes callbacks differently; the later VPW script and physical apron instructions describe the separate green controls.
mechanisms.label: Eight Flippers and Four Cabinet Buttons

mechanisms.behavior: Printed 39 switches main/cellar AC illumination through U and cuts playfield supply with T. Eight #313 lamps illuminate the cellar from the underside of the main playfield around the viewing glass; they are not a singleton floor light. Attic illumination, bumper lamps and lightbox name/scene lamps have separate physical branches. A11 is an autonomous 555/counter/decoder lightbox sequencer, not a bank of extra controller lamp callbacks. Physical socket positions/count reconciliation remain incomplete.
mechanisms.label: Three-Level Illumination and U Relay

Switches common playfield power and the match/ball-in-play lightbox branches; energized during play.
Interrupts the playfield AC GI and this game's controlled-lamp +6V DC; PinMAME does not emulate that DC cut. Tilt legend is on the other contact.

Lamp 2 is the coin-lockout circuit, not the attic first-target insert. The older script's local SetLamp100 drives a render light named L2; 100 is not a public lamp. PDF 29/printed 25 identifies Z1 Q3, A3 Q3 and A3J5-2; that driver region omits the winding and its wiring and supply. PDF 46/printed 42 traces wire 877 through A12J7/P7-8 to the front-door coil, whose other end is pin 7/wire 222; PDF 45/printed 41 identifies wire 222 as +24V DC. The winding part number remains unknown.

One Z1 Q4 latch and common A3 Q4 collector drive playboard L3 and lightbox L2 in parallel. Public 3 controls both; public 2 is the separate coin lockout. Only a proven playfield bulb would receive a placement.

A3J2-2/Q5 has no load named on this game's complete wiring or assignment pages, but the ROM pulses public 4 at ball serve as well as in the all-driver chase. The retained evidence does not explain that normal-play state. Fitment remains unknown; a test pulse is not proof of a fitted lamp.

Printed 25/26 and 31/32: public 9 is Sound16, the fifth sound-command bit, not illumination.
Printed 25/26 and 31/32: public 10 is Z3 Q3/high game to date (printed L11). ROM gameplay verifies lamp 10 during the high-score presentation.
Printed 25/26 and 31/32: public 11 is Z3 Q4/game over (printed L10). ROM gameplay verifies lamp 11 flashing in attract.
The L12 load is K relay; its normally open contact switches +38V DC onto the separate A-21741 cellar up-kicker coil. Project the effect onto SW31; do not call A-21741 a direct lamp-driver winding.
Lamp-driver control through booster Q3 (2N5875 or 2N5879) to the five-target reset. Projection onto the bank, not its winding centre.

Lamp-driver control through booster Q1 to the right-side kicking device; it is not an automatic shooter-lane plunger.

Lamp-driver control through booster Q2 to the hinged trap door. The local coil-side TRAP DOOR SW. contact is not matrix 36. No position sensor is published. Its effect is projected onto the world-mesh bounds of its own closed plate/linkage in retained VPW2.1, corroborated by the manual assembly and physical photo; this is not a winding-centre measurement or the primitive's stored pivot.

Selects main versus cellar illumination and flipper circuits; lamp 17=1 is the cellar interval in the script and ROM probe. Attic green-button flippers are separate hardware circuits. The relay's location is not a bulb coordinate.
